title: Seat picker and checkout UI
idea: The booking frontend is a seat picker and a checkout screen driven by one reducer, so the UI can never submit a hold or payment twice.
points: `SeatPicker` renders state and dispatches events; the reducer owns every rule.
Buttons disable while a request is in flight, and the reducer ignores repeats.
One Idempotency-Key per checkout survives retries, so a retry never charges twice.
Follow-ups: live seat updates, waitlists for sold-out shows, and seat map caching.

edges.label: owns
edges.caption: ShowPage owns the reducer state and passes it down. Children never keep their own copy.
In the PICKING step the page renders SeatPicker with the seat map from the API.
SeatGrid draws each seat and reports clicks as TOGGLE_SEAT events.

edges.label: hold
edges.caption: The hold button calls the API once; the step becomes HOLDING so repeat clicks do nothing.
After HOLD_OK the page shows CheckoutPanel and a HoldTimer for the deadline.
When the timer reaches zero it dispatches HOLD_EXPIRED and the user picks again.

edges.label: book
edges.caption: Pay sends POST /bookings with the checkout key; the service books the `show_seat` rows in one transaction.
The API returns 201, or 200 on a replay; both lead to the confirmation page.

walk.text: The whole screen state: step, chosen seats, hold, Idempotency-Key and error.
Seats toggle only while picking; a click clears the old error.
Hold starts once and only with seats chosen. HOLDING clears old errors and blocks a second click.
A 409 clears the selection; any other failure returns to picking with a retry message.
Pay is ignored unless PAYING. The key is made once, then reused; production uses a random UUID.
A failed payment goes back to PAYING but keeps the same key.
Hold expiry resets the screen, unless the booking is already done.

walk.text: Props bring the show, seats, reducer state, dispatch and the API client.
Mark HOLDING first, then call the API; 409 is a conflict, other failures return to picking.
No seat data yet means a loading state, never an empty grid.
Errors render in an alert region so screen readers announce them.
The button is disabled with no seats or once a hold is in flight.

pitfalls: Disabling a button is not enough; the reducer and the Idempotency-Key must also stop repeats.
Show the server's heldUntil, not a local ten-minute guess; clocks drift between devices.
Interview follow-up: polling the seat map at scale is costly; mention push updates or caching.

quiz.q: In the run, what is payKey after the payment retry?
quiz.why: PAY_CLICKED creates a key only when `payKey` is empty. PAY_FAILED keeps it, so the retry reuses ck-1.

takeaway: One reducer owns the screen; one key per checkout makes retries safe.
